vars.coverTitle: Marketing that helps buyers find what you build
vars.coverSub: Thorough, thoughtful inbound marketing for shops that make things, not brochures.
vars.whoTitle: Owners, GMs and the marketing department of one
vars.whoIntro: You're proud of the shop floor. The frustration is that pride doesn't show up when an engineer searches for what you build.
whoBullets: Owners and GMs at small-to-midsize, often multi-generation manufacturers.
VPs of Sales at bigger shops, usually first to say the website looks like 2012.
A marketing manager, if one exists, juggling trade shows and a Thomasnet listing.
Skeptical of any marketing spend they can't trace to a purchase order.
Assuming deals only come from trade shows or an existing relationship.
vars.brokenTitle: Here's where manufacturing marketing usually breaks

brokenItems.title: The website
brokenItems.body: Built like a brochure, not built to answer can this shop do the job.

brokenItems.title: Proof
brokenItems.body: Few or no case studies with a real number attached to a real deal.

brokenItems.title: Positioning
brokenItems.body: Quality, reliability, on-time delivery, said by every shop in the directory.

brokenItems.title: Lead capture
brokenItems.body: An RFQ form with no context, no phone number, no quick spec question.

brokenItems.title: Sales handoff
brokenItems.body: RFQs land in a shared inbox, nobody tracks what turned into a shipped part.

brokenItems.title: Attribution
brokenItems.body: No link between sponsoring a trade show and closing the account.

vars.journeyTitle: How your next customer is already searching

journeySteps.title: Trigger
journeySteps.body: A part, spec or deadline to fill

journeySteps.title: Search
journeySteps.body: A material, tolerance or cert term

journeySteps.title: RFQ
journeySteps.body: A quick question, then a quote

vars.journeyTakeaway: Thomasnet reports 1.4M monthly buyers actively sourcing suppliers online (business.thomasnet.com, 2026).

playItems.title: Capability pages
playItems.body: Specs, tolerances and materials, findable, not buried in a PDF.

playItems.title: Named case studies
playItems.body: A specific dollar figure tied to a specific deal, like BigOrange's own.

playItems.title: Certification pages
playItems.body: Checkable facts function as proof the way client logos do elsewhere.

playItems.title: A real RFQ flow
playItems.body: A path for a quick spec question, not just a full quote request.

playItems.title: CRM tagging
playItems.body: Every inbound RFQ tagged by source from the first click.

playItems.title: Attribution
playItems.body: A chain from spec search to closed account the owner can read.

proofStats.l: to a sales-qualified lead after launch (BigOrange)

vars.proofTakeaway: Named results from BigOrange's own manufacturing work, cited with the date fetched.
vars.plan1: Audit capabilities, the RFQ flow, and the search terms your buyers actually use.
vars.plan2: Turn PDFs into findable capability pages naming certs, tolerances and materials.
vars.plan3: Publish the first case study and route every RFQ into a CRM tagged by source.
vars.plan4: Review RFQ volume and quality together and decide what earns the next scope.
vars.investmentTitle: A bounded first engagement, then a scoped plan
vars.investmentIntro: No public pricing page exists on bigorange.marketing (checked 2026-09-02). Pricing is shared in the proposal, not guessed at here.
investmentBullets: First engagement is scoped and bounded, not an open-ended retainer.
Pricing is shared in the proposal once we've confirmed capabilities and access.
You approve every certification and capability claim before it publishes.
We propose the next scope only after the first one earns it.
vars.closeBody: One working session to map the capability pages, the RFQ flow and the first case study.

proof.notes: Sources: BigOrange manufacturing hub page, bigorange.marketing/manufacturing-services-marketing-agency/, fetched 2026-09-02 ($150K organic deal, sales-qualified lead day after launch, 50+ reviews).
